about_your_time.body: Six quantum gravity chats form one continuous arc — each opens with a summary you dictated, each picks up mid-sentence from the last, and the framework version number carries forward.
about_your_time.title: You're building a single structure across sessions, not browsing.

about_your_time.body: Penrose diagrams got a from-scratch rebuild when the Session 4 treatment felt schematic; conjugates got three nested passes (complex, frequency, operator) before you said the word 'understand'; the entanglement wedge got four separate re-explanations before you moved on.
about_your_time.title: You stop and rebuild when something isn't solid.

about_your_time.body: The de Sitter thread lives in its own conversation, the Bogoliubov follow-up stayed in the Session 3 chat, and the paper analyses each got a dedicated window — you're keeping context boundaries clean without being told to.
about_your_time.title: You route yourself to the right chat.

expanding_your_skills.body: You'd hand off derivations and paper retrieval — the Bogoliubov coefficient calculation, the arXiv fetches for the naked-black-hole and nanoconfined-water papers — then decide which thread to follow next, when to start a new chat, and what to put in each session summary.
expanding_your_skills.title: Research and explanation go to Claude; structural decisions stay with you.

expanding_your_skills.body: Session 4 opened with the full Session 3 summary plus the supplementary continuation summary, then 'I want to understand what happens in an expanding de Sitter universe.' Session 3 opened with 'I want to title this chat' and a thread selection. A project holding the running summary and the v3.7.1 framework would let each session start without the paste.
expanding_your_skills.title: Every deep-dive session opens with the same move: a pasted summary and a stated destination.

expanding_your_skills.body: You stopped the de Sitter session to say 'still really don't know much about Penrose diagrams'; you stopped the entanglement-wedge discussion to ask about the anchoring of the minimal surface; you stopped the Bogoliubov discussion to say 'I really want to understand about conjugates, I've tried multiple times.'
expanding_your_skills.title: You flag what you don't understand before moving on.

expanding_your_skills.body: Each summary carries forward your profile ('chemistry degree from the 1970s, 25 years as Intel performance engineer'), the framework version, the open threads, and the explicit next-session destination — so the next chat can verify continuity rather than re-derive it.
expanding_your_skills.title: The session summaries you write are the record of what you've learned.

content.hero_body: Most of June went into a single, sustained project: a multi-session deep dive through the foundations of quantum gravity, from effective field theory through AdS/CFT, the information paradox, holographic codes, and de Sitter holography. Each session ran long — three hours was typical — and each one picked up exactly where the last left off, with summaries you wrote yourself bridging the gaps. Two astrophysics papers got the full framework treatment alongside the physics. The way you used Claude this month was almost entirely as a tutor you could interrupt, redirect, and push back on.
